notes: Identity verified from the supplied canonical text: title Collaboration Promotes Proportional Reasoning about Resource Distribution in Young Children; authors Rowena Ng, Gail D Heyman, David Barner; DOI 10.1037/a0024923; Dev Psychol. 2011 Sep;47(5):1230–1238. This is a primary author manuscript hosted in PMC with study methods/results and references, rather than an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF was supplied. Study 1 and the niceness-comparison outcome are established, but the neutral description and p.3 locator do not distinguish the age main effect across both trial types (F(2, 27) = 31.88, p < .001), the age-by-trial-type interaction (F(2, 27) = 27.10, p < .001), the conflict-trial age omnibus (F(2, 29) = 62.05, p < .001), and the five-year-old/adult Tukey contrasts. The overall age follow-up and conflict-trial follow-up each report p < .001 for adults versus five-year-olds, without a printed pairwise test statistic. The F tests include seven-year-olds and cannot be relabelled as a five-year-old/adult pairwise statistic. No candidate is selected. Candidate participant counts only: mutually exclusive Study 1 groups are 8 five-year-olds, 8 seven-year-olds and 14 adults. A pairwise five-year-old/adult comparison would involve 8 + 14 = 22 participants; three-age omnibus models would involve 8 + 8 + 14 = 30 participants. The procedure identifies the same subjects across tasks; no Study 1 exclusions are stated in the inspected Subjects, Procedure, and Results sections. These are candidate group sums, not an assigned analytic N, because the critical test is unresolved. No N is inferred from degrees of freedom. Only n_r and es_value_r assigned; other fields are unassigned placeholders.
